Subject: Potential exposure affecting EU subset — notification timeline & subprocessor access

Hi Nikhil / Priyom,

We detected an anomalous export from one of our integration endpoints this morning that appears to include snippets of user-generated content tied to EU residents. At a glance it looks scoped (estimated ~120 affected IDs) but we're still validating. We need to coordinate notification obligations under our DPA and determine whether we must request forensics access to Redwood subprocessor logs and raw request payloads.

Can you confirm:
- Redwood's standard incident-notification timeline for DPAs when EU personal data is plausibly involved (we need the contractual baseline and any operational SLAs you follow)
- Whether Redwood will permit a scoped evidence export (logs + request metadata) to a mutually agreed SFTP or signed escrow mechanism; if so, what documentation/requests you require (legal POA, signed data access request, redaction rules)
- Whether any cross-border movement of data would occur during the collection and what safeguards you apply (pseudonymization/encryption/transit controls)

I've attached the initial_indicator_summary.csv and a short list of the fields we think may be included. Jordan from OrchardHealth (copied on this thread) is our security lead on the integration and will assist with triage.

We need to get a working plan within 48 hours to meet our regulatory timeline and to scope notifications. Appreciate a prompt confirmation of next steps and the internal contacts you want engaged.

Thanks,
Emma Lopez
Head of Security Operations
Clearwater Systems

Subject: Re: Potential exposure affecting EU subset — notification timeline & subprocessor access

Emma — thanks for the heads up and for the data you attached. High-level response and proposed next steps below.

1) Notification baseline: per our DPA (section 6.2) Redwood notifies customers "without undue delay" and commits to a measurable operational target of confirmation of internal scope within 48 hours of receiving a validated indicator; we then provide a formal incident notice with a proposed remediation/timeline within 72 hours. For EU-resident data we follow the same baseline but add the jurisdictional routing checklist and legal review step — that add-on tends to extend final remediation timelines, which is why we surface an interim notice early.

2) Evidence access: Redwood supports scoped evidence exports for substantiated requests. We require: (a) a signed Data Access Request (template in our Ops library), (b) explicit per-record markers for the export scope (IDs or timestamp windows), and (c) agreement on redaction rules for PII in transit. Once we have (a)-(c) legal will review and operations will schedule a timeboxed export to an SFTP managed by the customer or to our secure escrow endpoint (we use client-specific encryption keys).

3) Cross-border movement: any export of raw logs that includes EU personal data will be carried under our standard transfer safeguards. Options: pseudonymized export (recommended), encrypted archive with customer-managed key, or on-site viewing via secure console session (no long-term transfer). If the export includes cleartext EU identifiers, we will route the transfer through our EU region hosts where feasible to limit cross-border flow; if not feasible, we apply our SCCs + technical encryption for transit.

Immediate asks from you: please confirm the exact ID list or a tight timestamp window and who will sign the Data Access Request (name, title, email). From our side I'll loop in Ben (for operations/forensics) and Laura (legal) to get a fast-track review. We aim to provide a scoped timeline within 24 hours after we get the ID window.

I'll also attach our jurisdiction routing matrix and a short evidence manifest template for your legal team.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Security Lead
Redwood Inference

Looping in operational specifics. Quick notes:
- We can produce a timeboxed evidence export (logs + request metadata + worker traces) scoped to the ID list or the timestamp window you provide. Typical turnaround for schedule (once legal signoff exists) is 24–48 hours; export generation takes ~2–6 hours depending on the size of the logs.
- For cross-border protections: we will default to a pseudonymized export or provide a client-managed-key encrypted archive. We do not perform live transfers to third-party cloud buckets without an executed access addendum.
- Subprocessor access: if Clearwater's forensics team requires direct query capability against our internal indices we require a formal Subprocessor Access Request and either (i) a supervised onsite/VM session or (ii) an executed limited-scope API token with audit hooks. This is to satisfy our subprocessor obligations and to keep a clear audit trail.

Operational POC for scheduling: ben.carter@redwood.ai. Legal intake: laura.bennett@redwood.ai. Please send the signed Data Access Request and the exact scope, and we'll provision a secure workspace or export.

Ben Carter

If you can put a brief interim notice in the format of your standard DPA template within 24 hours of our signed request, that would help us meet our disclosure timeline.
